{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implementation instructions for frontend engineers:

Goal: Stop relying on or sending a title field. The API responses will no longer include title; use name only. Do not add new fallbacks that rely on unspecified server behavior.

Steps:
1) Find all places in the client codebase that read, display, or use response.title (or similar). This includes view code, components, helpers, selectors, and any code that builds request payloads.
2) Remove fallback logic that reads response.title when name is absent. Replace it with direct use of response.name. Do not introduce a new fallback that assumes any other server field; if name is missing, show the existing empty/unknown UI state (or the current placeholder behavior) rather than attempting to read title.
3) Update client API types/interfaces (e.g., TypeScript interfaces, response DTOs) so that server response types do not include title. Do not change any other field names or types (description, id, owner_id, created_at must remain). Do not rename fields that map to the database.
4) Ensure the client does not include a title property in outgoing request payloads. Audit request construction code and remove any code that sets title. This prevents triggering the server's 422 behavior for requests that include title.
5) Tests:
   - Update unit tests and component tests to remove expectations about title in responses and UI.
   - Add or update tests asserting the client uses response.name for display and payload construction.
   - Add tests (or adapt existing API-integration/e2e tests) to verify the client will not send title in requests and that network responses contain name (and do not contain title).
6) QA / Verification steps before merge:
   - Run end-to-end tests and inspect actual network responses to ensure title is absent and name is present.
   - Manually attempt to send a request including title (e.g., via devtools) and confirm the server returns 422; ensure the client code does not generate such requests by default.
7) Code review checklist:
   - No remaining references to .title in response-reading codepaths.
   - API response types updated to exclude title.
   - No code path sets title on outgoing requests.

Do not change any backend or database schema in the frontend changes. If any ambiguity remains about which endpoints/response types to change, locate them by searching the codebase for usages of the string "title" in code that treats it as an API response property and work only on those occurrences."
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implementation instructions for backend engineers:

Goal: Stop emitting title in all public API responses; continue to reject requests that include title with HTTP 422; do not rename or remove the database column for title (no DB migrations that change column name).

Steps:
1) Locate all serializers/DTOs/response mappers/handlers that currently include the title field in outgoing JSON across the public API surface. This includes list endpoints, item endpoints, and any endpoints that return objects containing the title field.
2) Remove title from the serialized/outgoing representation so JSON responses no longer contain the title property. Implementation options (choose what matches your stack):
   - If you use explicit response DTOs/serializers, remove title from the DTO.
   - If you use model->JSON helpers (e.g., toJSON), exclude title from the output there.
   - If you use automatic schema generation (OpenAPI/GraphQL/resolvers), update the response schemas to not include title in responses.
Important: Do not rename the database column or change storage. The database field for title must remain unchanged per constraint.

3) Preserve request validation behavior: continue to detect client requests that include a title property and respond with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity. If this validation already exists, leave it intact. If it does not exist, implement explicit validation that returns 422 when a client-supplied payload contains a title key (even if null). Do not alter this behavior.

4) API specification and docs:
   - Update any OpenAPI/Swagger/REST docs to remove title from response schemas.
   - Keep any documentation about title in internal DB or admin endpoints separate if applicable; do not document title in public response schemas.

5) Tests:
   - Add/modify unit tests for serializers/response mappers to assert that the serialized output does not include title and still includes name, description, id, owner_id, created_at, etc.
   - Add/modify integration tests for each affected endpoint to verify responses contain no title field.
   - Add/modify tests that assert requests containing title result in HTTP 422.
   - Add a regression test ensuring no database schema migration or code change renames/deletes the title column.

6) Backward-compatibility and deployment notes:
   - This is a breaking change for consumers that expected title in responses. Coordinate with the frontend team and update API versioning / changelog per your standard release process if required by policy. (Do not invent new contract semantics here; follow existing versioning policies.)

7) Verification checklist before merge:
   - Run automated test suite (unit + integration) confirming responses lack title and that requests with title return 422.
   - Inspect generated OpenAPI/spec files to confirm response schemas removed title.
   - Confirm no DB migration renames/removes the title column and that database queries still select the title column if ORM models reference it internally (but keep it out of public responses).

Do not make assumptions about which endpoints to change beyond: any endpoint that currently includes title in public JSON responses must be updated. If you cannot discover all occurrences, perform a codebase search for the string "title" used in response/serializer contexts and update those matches."
  }
}
